segments.he: עַל יְדֵי הַתְּפִלָּה נֶחְשָׁב כְּאִלּוּ עָשָׂה מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת
segments.en: And as long as a person is not firm in his resolve to always hope to Hashem and entreat Him even if whatever comes upon him, his teshuvah is still not complete — for who knows what the day will bring? Perhaps a test or stumbling will come upon him. But if a person is firm in his resolve that even if, Heaven forbid, he does not stand firm in the test — even so he will always hope to Hashem — in the aspect of "if I make my bed in the depths, there You are" — then he is certain that he will certainly merit complete teshuvah. For in the end he will return to Hashem, since he is firm in his resolve not to fall from anything in the world. And as we heard from Rabbainu of blessed memory himself, who said to us explicitly: "As you see me" — meaning, you know my great holiness, that I am a complete Tzaddik — "even so, if I were now to commit an actual great transgression, I would not fall in my resolve at all. Rather I would be an upright person after the transgression as before — only afterward I would do teshuvah." And therefore the first redemption is the aspect of Torah — for then Yisrael merited to receive the Torah. And the final redemption is the aspect of prayer, as Rabbainu of blessed memory wrote [Likutay Moharan I:2] — for Moshiach will build the Holy Temple for us, which is the place of prayer, as it is written: "for My house shall be called a house of prayer" [Yeshayahu 56:7]. This is the aspect of Moshiach ben Dovid — for Dovid is the aspect of the totality of the prayer of the upright of Yisrael who pray to Hashem to merit returning to Him in truth. For he is the ne'im zemiros Yisrael [sweet singer of Yisrael], and all prayers are called by his name — for the entire Book of Tehillim that King Dovid composed was founded upon this matter: that we merit to return to Him from all the falls in the world. For there is no wisdom and no understanding and no counsel to stand against the adversary except through prayer — through which one merits all the counsels and all the forms of salvation, to merit emerging from the exile of one's soul and drawing close to Him.

segments.he: וְעַל כֵּן תּוֹקְעִין שׁוֹפָר וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין מַלְכֻיּוֹת וְכוּ' הַכּל בִּתְפִלַּת מוּסָף. כִּי תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף מִתְפַּלְּלִין רַק עַל הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁהָיִינוּ צְרִיכִין לְהַקְרִיב בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ. וּבַעֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ חָרֵב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ. וְאֵין אָנוּ יְכוֹלִין לְהַקְרִיב קָרְבָּן וְכוּ'. עַל כֵּן אָנוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִין לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁנִּזְכֶּה לְהַקְרִיב הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים וּמִפְּנֵי חֲטָאֵינוּ וְכוּ' וְשָׁם נַעֲשֶׂה וְנַקְרִיב לְפָנֶיךָ וְכוּ' וְאֶת מוּסַף יוֹם וְכוּ' נִמְצָא שֶׁתְּפִלַּת מוּסָף הִוא בְּחִינַת שֶׁעוֹשִׂין מִתּוֹרָה תְּפִלָּה דְּהַיְנוּ מֵהַמִּצְוָה שֶׁל הַקְרָבַת הַקָּרְבַּן מוּסָף עוֹשִׂין מִזֶּה תְּפִלָּה וּבָזֶה אָנוּ מַמְשִׁיכִין הַדֶּרֶךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת מִתּוֹרוֹת תְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁהִוא גַּם כֵּן בִּבְחִינָה זוֹ שֶׁל תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא רָחוֹק מִקִּיּוּם אֵיזֶה מִצְוָה הֵן מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה אוֹ לא תַעֲשֶׂה צָרִיךְ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְקַיְּמָהּ שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַמָּשׁ תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף שֶׁמִּתְפַּלְּלִין שֶׁנִּזְכֶּה לְקַיֵּם מַה שֶּׁאֵין אָנוּ יְכוֹלִין לְקַיֵּם עַתָּה בַּעֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ בְּעֵת הַחֻרְבָּן. וְזאת הַתְּפִלָּה נֶחְשֶׁבֶת בִּמְקוֹם קָרְבָּן. וְגַם עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִזְכֶּה סוֹף כָּל סוֹף לָשׁוּב לְאַרְצֵנוּ וּלְהַקְרִיב שָׁם קָרְבְּנוֹת חוֹבוֹתֵינוּ כְּמוֹ כֵן הוּא מַמָּשׁ הַתְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁעוֹשִׂין מִתּוֹרוֹת שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הַרְבֵּה שֶׁנִּזְכֶּה לְקַיֵּם מַה שֶּׁקָּשֶׁה לָנוּ לְקַיֵּם עַתָּה בַּעֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ בְּתֹקֶף גָּלוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ.
segments.en: As long as a person has not merited complete prayer, he still has no place before Hashem and is still a wanderer and vagrant and uprooted. And even if he engages in Torah, he is still not certain that he will remain established in his position — for who knows what will come upon him? As we have seen with many people who engaged in Torah with great diligence for many years and afterward fell greatly and distanced themselves from Torah entirely. And especially since there are many people who fell to wherever they fell — some even to actual great transgressions, Heaven have mercy — and they are sunk in the mire and the mud. And they hope and yearn to emerge from their filth and impurity, but there is none to save them and extract them.

segments.he: וְעַל יְדֵי תְּפִלּוֹת אֵלּוּ נִזְכֶּה לְבַסּוֹף לָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְגַם כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ זוֹכִין עֲדַיִן לִגְאֻלַּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת יִהְיֶה נֶחְשָׁב לָנוּ עַל יְדֵי הַתְּפִלָּה כְּאִלּוּ קִיַּמְנוּ וְעָשִׂינוּ מַה שֶּׁמֻּטָּל עָלֵינוּ.
segments.en: Therefore the primary place and standing in holiness is prayer — for through prayer one merits to remain always established in one's position, even whatever may come. For when one has merited only Torah alone — though this is very good and is the primary purpose, for it is our life and the length of our days — even so, when one falls, Heaven forbid, from Torah, one has nothing with which to revive oneself. But when one has merited prayer, one has hope forever, even whatever comes upon one. For sometimes a person falls to a deep descent where there is no standing at all — especially in these generations where many in Yisrael have fallen greatly until they are in their own eyes past all hope. About them King Dovid prophesied: "I sank in the mire of the depths and there was no foothold; I came into deep waters and a flood overwhelmed me" [Tehillim 69:3]. For about this exile it is said: "she has fallen wondrously; there is none to comfort her" [Eichah 1:9]. And the great pity for people like this who are sinking in the mire and there is no standing — it is beyond measure. May the Omnipresent have mercy upon them. And how is it possible to revive oneself and remain standing in such a fall and descent where there is no standing at all, being distanced from all holiness and sinking and drowning each day further? Therefore the primary thing is prayer and crying and sighing to Hashem. As Dovid said there, after describing at length the great distress of soul that is upon each person in Yisrael according to his situation — the aspect of "I sank in the mire of the depths and there was no foothold" — "I wearied myself calling... they who hate me without cause are more than the hairs of my head." Afterward he said: "but as for me, my prayer is to You, Hashem, at an acceptable time" [Tehillim 69:14] — that I will hold myself always in prayer and supplication to Hashem, perhaps He will have compassion. For prayer is the aspect of standing and place, even in the mire of the depths where there is no standing. For prayer is called amidah [standing] — for there is amidah only in prayer, as our Rabbis taught [Berachos 6b]. And as it is written: "our feet were standing in your gates, O Jerusalem" [Tehillim 122:2] — for in Jerusalem was the Holy Temple which is the house of prayer — there is the primary aspect of amidah. For through prayer one can always draw close to Hashem even as one is. For even though one is far from all holiness and all Torah and can revive oneself through nothing — even so, if one lifts one's eyes above and prays to Hashem from wherever one is, one still has hope. Therefore one who wishes to be a true Yisraeli must hold fast to both Torah and prayer — for both together are good, so that if one falls, Heaven forbid, the one will raise the other.

segments.he: נִמְצָא שֶׁתְּפִלַּת מוּסָף הִוא בִּבְחִינַת תְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁעוֹשִׂין מִתּוֹרוֹת עַל כֵּן אָז תּוֹקְעִין בְּשׁוֹפָר וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין מַלְכֻיּוֹת וְכוּ'. כִּי שׁוֹפָר וּמַלְכֻיּוֹת וְזִכְרוֹנוֹת וְכוּ' הֵם בִּשְׁבִיל בְּחִינַת זאת לִזְכּוֹת לְהָקִים אֶת הַתְּפִלָּה לַעֲשׂוֹת מִתּוֹרוֹת תְּפִלּוֹת כַּנַּ"ל. שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף כַּנַּ"ל. (שָׁם אוֹת י):
segments.en: When one merits prayer as described above — meaning the person is resolute and courageous in his resolve to always pray to Hashem to draw him close to His service in truth, whatever may be, in the aspect of "I will always hope" [Tehillim 71:14] — then certainly the evil inclination can no longer deceive or mislead him in any way, in the aspect of: "there is no [law of] wrongful deception for real property." For prayer is the aspect of the final redemption that has no interruption after it, as above — in the aspect of semichas ge'ulah litfilah [adjoining redemption to prayer]: for the primary attachment of the general and individual redemption is to prayer. For our primary hope and support for complete redemption speedily in our days — in the general and individual sense — is through prayer. For whatever the situation, as long as one strengthens and fortifies one's heart to still pray to Hashem to return one to Him, and spreads one's hands to Hashem from wherever one is — even if many days and years pass in one's corruption, each according to what one is caught in — even so, as long as one is still praying, one has support and hope and standing through prayer and supplication and entreaties even in the mire of the depths where there is no standing. As it is written: "I put my hope in Hashem; He inclined to me and heard my cry. He raised me from the pit of desolation, from the miry bog; He set my feet upon a rock and made my steps firm" [Tehillim 40:2–3] — for through constantly crying and calling to Hashem with hope after hope, I merited: "He raised me from the pit of desolation, from the miry bog" — rising from very bad and impure places called pit of desolation and miry bog, where there is no standing when one falls there and one could, Heaven forbid, drown there. But I who hoped to Hashem with hope after hope and called to Hashem always — through this He raised me up and "set my feet upon a rock and made my steps firm." For the primary standing and establishment and support is through prayer to Hashem — for through prayer and crying and imploring to Hashem one can stand even in a place where there is no standing at all. And as long as a person has not merited complete prayer — even if he engages in Torah, which is the primary purpose — even so he is still not safe from the deceptions and errors of the adversary. But when one merits prayer as above, one is safe from all deceptions and errors forever — for over everything one will pray to Hashem always, however things are. And this is the aspect of the final redemption that has no interruption after it, as above.

aligned_segments.en: And they hope and yearn to emerge from their filth and impurity, but there is none to save them and extract them.

aligned_segments.he: וְעַל יְדֵי תְּפִלּוֹת אֵלּוּ נִזְכֶּה לְבַסּוֹף לָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ.
aligned_segments.en: Therefore the primary place and standing in holiness is prayer — for through prayer one merits to remain always established in one's position, even whatever may come. For when one has merited only Torah alone — though this is very good and is the primary purpose, for it is our life and the length of our days — even so, when one falls, Heaven forbid, from Torah, one has nothing with which to revive oneself. But when one has merited prayer, one has hope forever, even whatever comes upon one. For sometimes a person falls to a deep descent where there is no standing at all — especially in these generations where many in Yisrael have fallen greatly until they are in their own eyes past all hope. About them King Dovid prophesied: "I sank in the mire of the depths and there was no foothold; I came into deep waters and a flood overwhelmed me" [Tehillim 69:3]. For about this exile it is said: "she has fallen wondrously; there is none to comfort her" [Eichah 1:9]. And the great pity for people like this who are sinking in the mire and there is no standing — it is beyond measure. May the Omnipresent have mercy upon them.

aligned_segments.he: וְגַם כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ זוֹכִין עֲדַיִן לִגְאֻלַּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת יִהְיֶה נֶחְשָׁב לָנוּ עַל יְדֵי הַתְּפִלָּה כְּאִלּוּ קִיַּמְנוּ וְעָשִׂינוּ מַה שֶּׁמֻּטָּל עָלֵינוּ.
aligned_segments.en: And how is it possible to revive oneself and remain standing in such a fall and descent where there is no standing at all, being distanced from all holiness and sinking and drowning each day further? Therefore the primary thing is prayer and crying and sighing to Hashem. As Dovid said there, after describing at length the great distress of soul that is upon each person in Yisrael according to his situation — the aspect of "I sank in the mire of the depths and there was no foothold" — "I wearied myself calling... they who hate me without cause are more than the hairs of my head." Afterward he said: "but as for me, my prayer is to You, Hashem, at an acceptable time" [Tehillim 69:14] — that I will hold myself always in prayer and supplication to Hashem, perhaps He will have compassion. For prayer is the aspect of standing and place, even in the mire of the depths where there is no standing. For prayer is called amidah [standing] — for there is amidah only in prayer, as our Rabbis taught [Berachos 6b]. And as it is written: "our feet were standing in your gates, O Jerusalem" [Tehillim 122:2] — for in Jerusalem was the Holy Temple which is the house of prayer — there is the primary aspect of amidah. For through prayer one can always draw close to Hashem even as one is. For even though one is far from all holiness and all Torah and can revive oneself through nothing — even so, if one lifts one's eyes above and prays to Hashem from wherever one is, one still has hope. Therefore one who wishes to be a true Yisraeli must hold fast to both Torah and prayer — for both together are good, so that if one falls, Heaven forbid, the one will raise the other.

aligned_segments.he: נִמְצָא שֶׁתְּפִלַּת מוּסָף הִוא בִּבְחִינַת תְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁעוֹשִׂין מִתּוֹרוֹת עַל כֵּן אָז תּוֹקְעִין בְּשׁוֹפָר וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין מַלְכֻיּוֹת וְכוּ'.
aligned_segments.en: When one merits prayer as described above — meaning the person is resolute and courageous in his resolve to always pray to Hashem to draw him close to His service in truth, whatever may be, in the aspect of "I will always hope" [Tehillim 71:14] — then certainly the evil inclination can no longer deceive or mislead him in any way, in the aspect of: "there is no [law of] wrongful deception for real property." For prayer is the aspect of the final redemption that has no interruption after it, as above — in the aspect of semichas ge'ulah litfilah [adjoining redemption to prayer]: for the primary attachment of the general and individual redemption is to prayer. For our primary hope and support for complete redemption speedily in our days — in the general and individual sense — is through prayer. For whatever the situation, as long as one strengthens and fortifies one's heart to still pray to Hashem to return one to Him, and spreads one's hands to Hashem from wherever one is — even if many days and years pass in one's corruption, each according to what one is caught in — even so, as long as one is still praying, one has support and hope and standing through prayer and supplication and entreaties even in the mire of the depths where there is no standing.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי שׁוֹפָר וּמַלְכֻיּוֹת וְזִכְרוֹנוֹת וְכוּ' הֵם בִּשְׁבִיל בְּחִינַת זאת לִזְכּוֹת לְהָקִים אֶת הַתְּפִלָּה לַעֲשׂוֹת מִתּוֹרוֹת תְּפִלּוֹת כַּנַּ"ל.
aligned_segments.en: As it is written: "I put my hope in Hashem; He inclined to me and heard my cry. He raised me from the pit of desolation, from the miry bog; He set my feet upon a rock and made my steps firm" [Tehillim 40:2–3] — for through constantly crying and calling to Hashem with hope after hope, I merited: "He raised me from the pit of desolation, from the miry bog" — rising from very bad and impure places called pit of desolation and miry bog, where there is no standing when one falls there and one could, Heaven forbid, drown there. But I who hoped to Hashem with hope after hope and called to Hashem always — through this He raised me up and "set my feet upon a rock and made my steps firm." For the primary standing and establishment and support is through prayer to Hashem — for through prayer and crying and imploring to Hashem one can stand even in a place where there is no standing at all.

aligned_segments.he: שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף כַּנַּ"ל. (שָׁם אוֹת י):
aligned_segments.en: And as long as a person has not merited complete prayer — even if he engages in Torah, which is the primary purpose — even so he is still not safe from the deceptions and errors of the adversary. But when one merits prayer as above, one is safe from all deceptions and errors forever — for over everything one will pray to Hashem always, however things are. And this is the aspect of the final redemption that has no interruption after it, as above.
